item.title: Said & Checked, Illinois, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Dick Durbin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator: “the only two countries in the world that allow drug companies to advertise their product.” Unsettled. Researchers writing in The Conversation (2024) say the U.S. and New Zealand are the only high-income countries allowing unrestricted direct-to-consumer advertising of branded medicines, while noting Canada permits limited reminder ads; no official source was read.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator: “virtually all of these drugs that have come to market started with Federal research at the National Institute of Health.” Unsettled. Cleary and colleagues (PNAS 2018) found NIH funding contributed to published research associated with all 210 new drugs FDA approved in 2010-2016, but more than 90% of that funding was basic research on biological targets rather than on the drugs, so "started with" fits only in that broad sense.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator: “29 percent of high school students in America were smoking tobacco cigarettes--29 percent; today, 2 percent--2 percent--smoking tobacco cigarettes.” Unsettled. CDC's youth tobacco survey shows 1.7% of high school students smoking cigarettes in 2024, matching the 2 percent figure, but CDC's earlier surveys show 27.5% in 1991, a 36.4% peak in 1997 and 28.5% in 2001, so the 29 percent starting figure fits only some years.

item.title: Said & Checked, Illinois, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 2 unsettled (Dick Durbin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “81 percent of Americans support citizenship for Dreamers, including 56 percent of Republicans.” Unsupported. No poll was found reporting both 81% of Americans and 56% of Republicans supporting citizenship for Dreamers. The American Immigration Council's 2018 survey has an 81% figure only for a subgroup of conservative and Republican voters. Searched: the AskAmerica catalog (no polling tables), that survey, and web search results pointing to polls with different wording (legal status rather than citizenship) that were not opened.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “Paul Ryan refused to call it or amend it or consider it.” Unsettled. S. 744 died in the House in the 113th Congress, when John Boehner was Speaker; Boehner and House Republicans said it would not get a floor vote (as compiled by Wikipedia). Paul Ryan became Speaker in October 2015. No primary record was read, and the statement may refer to later Dreamer legislation.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “I have come to the floor of the Senate over 150 times to share the stories of Dreamers” Unsettled. In the same Nov. 17 speech Durbin calls it his '154th Dreamer story', but that is his own running count; no independent tally of his floor speeches was found, and the warehouse has no floor-speech data.

item.title: Said & Checked, Illinois, 2026-11-17: none false or contradicted, 2 unsupported, 9 unsettled (Dick Durbin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “we heard from two nominees who have been out of law school for just 8 years. One of them has practiced law for just 7 years; the other has only practiced for 5 years.” Unsupported. No source giving the nominees' law school graduation or years of practice was found. The search covered the committee's Nov. 10 hearing page and two of the five nominees' questionnaires, which are scanned images with no readable text, plus a web search; the other three questionnaires and press coverage were not read.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “That is less experience than any Biden nominee or any prior Trump nominee.” Unsupported. No comparison of these nominees' experience against all Biden and earlier Trump judicial nominees was found; the speaker's own Nov. 10 statement compares them with nominees heard by the committee in the last 10 years. The search covered the Congressional Record, the committee's Nov. 10 press release and coverage of that hearing; ABA ratings data and the Federal Judicial Center's biographical records were not searched.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “This month, Republicans are holding nominations hearings 8 days apart, holding hearings for nominees whose Senate Judiciary questionnaires were received just days beforehand, and holding hearings with as many as eight nominees.” Unsettled. The committee's hearings list shows nomination hearings on Nov. 10 and Nov. 18, eight days apart. The Nov. 10 hearing had five nominees and no November hearing with eight was found; the nominees' questionnaire receipt dates could not be read.
